BERT4Rec trains masked-item predictions with full-catalog softmax cross-entropy; inference appends a reserved mask token. The original paper also includes training examples with only the final item masked, supporting a combined random-mask/terminal-mask objective within one model. Keep terminal targets absent from the bidirectional input. Reproducibility work found original defaults could undertrain substantially: matching reported results required up to 30× longer training, while an optimized implementation reduced convergence time by up to 95%. These figures describe specific implementations and datasets, not expected RecHarness runtime. [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.06690v2), [replicability study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.07483).

Full-softmax cost depends on supervised positions, not necessarily every sequence position. Engineering inference: gathering M masked hidden states before projection produces M×V logits, with projection work O(MVd). At M=1,024 and V=50,000, logits alone occupy about 195 MiB in float32; gradients, temporary buffers, embeddings and optimizer states add memory. Two separately corrupted sequence views also require extra encoder computation. The original implementation gathers prediction positions before vocabulary projection and normalizes loss by valid masked-target weight. For two objectives, average each over its valid targets before applying an explicit mixing weight, avoiding accidental weighting by mask count. [Original implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/master/run.py).

Changing to sampled softmax alongside terminal masking would confound attribution: it changes the denominator and training gradients, with results depending on negative count, sampling distribution and correction. Loss-comparison research shows loss choice materially affects recommendation quality. First compare masking objectives with identical full softmax; investigate sampling separately if measured memory or runtime requires it. [Loss-comparison study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.07602).
